3.1.1.locator: GDPR resource center, encryption-in-transit passage: 'applied by default on Google Cloud to encrypt requests before transmission and to protect the raw data using the Transport Layer Security (TLS) protocol'
3.1.1.notes: VERIFIER CONFIRMED 2026-07-31: quote found verbatim on the fetched GDPR page. Independently re-checked for version numbers: zero matches for any 'TLS 1.x' string across the full fetched text of the GDPR page, the Cloud DPA, and the Service Terms — so the versioned dropdown options (TLS 1.2/1.3) genuinely cannot be selected from these sources, and 'Others - pls indicate below' (real standard: TLS, version unstated) is the correct conservative choice. The 'Encryption in transit' whitepaper that documents versions lives on docs.cloud.google.com, which is policy-blocked by this sandbox's gateway (403 CONNECT, re-confirmed this session). A human with normal network access should confirm the TLS version from https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/security/encryption-in-transit before submission and upgrade this cell to TLS 1.2 or 1.3 if stated. Free-text indication to accompany the dropdown: 'TLS (Transport Layer Security), applied by default; version not stated in Google's DPA/GDPR pages.'

3.1.2.notes: VERIFIER: 'Not known' KEPT after independent check 2026-07-31. Mandatory independent WebSearch could not run (session budget exhausted, 200/200); instead directly probed candidate primary sources on reachable hosts: (a) https://cloud.google.com/trust-center/security fetched — no algorithm stated (only 'encrypt customer content stored at rest, without any action required by you'); (b) Cloud DPA fetched — its only AES statement ('using at least AES128 or similar') sits verbatim inside the Google Distributed Cloud connected section, confirming the researcher's note that it is product-specific, not general GCP; (c) the 'Default encryption at rest' whitepaper redirects to docs.cloud.google.com which the sandbox gateway policy-denies (403 CONNECT, re-confirmed via curl and WebFetch this session). Encryption-at-rest-by-default IS confirmed on the GDPR page, but no reachable primary source states the algorithm, so 'Not known' stands. Human action: fetch https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/security/encryption/default-encryption from an unrestricted network (it documents AES-256) and upgrade this cell.

3.1.3.notes: VERIFIER: 'Not known' KEPT after independent check 2026-07-31. Same constraints as 3.1.2 (WebSearch budget exhausted; docs.cloud.google.com blocked). 3.1.8.locator: Cloud DPA Appendix 2 (Security Measures); also https://cloud.google.com/privacy/gdpr (Encryption, Access Controls, Incident Management, Disaster Recovery Testing sections), https://cloud.google.com/security/products/security-key-management, https://cloud.google.com/terms/service-terms (Data Location; Assured Workloads)
3.1.8.notes:
downgraded from 'Encryption in transit by default using the TLS protocol (Cloud DPA Appendix 2; GDPR resource center)
Encryption at rest by default without customer action (GDPR resource center)
Perfect forward secrecy: ephemeral elliptic-curve Diffie-Hellman key exchange signed with RSA and ECDSA (Cloud DPA Appendix 2, 'Encryption Technologies')
Logical isolation of customer data in a multi-tenant environment on Google-owned servers (Cloud DPA Appendix 2, Section 3(a) 'Data Storage, Isolation and Logging')
Least-privilege, need-to-know access controls for Google personnel; formal approval process for additional access; hardware tokens for access to extremely sensitive information (GDPR resource center; Cloud DPA Appendix 2)
Data center physical security: on-site security operation responsible for all physical data center security functions 24 hours a day, 7 days a week; CCTV cameras inside and outside the data centers monitored by on-site security; electronic card key access with alarms linked to the on-site security operation; regular internal and external patrols; alarmed fire doors (Cloud DPA Appendix 2, Section 2(a))
Full Disk Encryption (FDE) and drive locking on hard drives; asset tracking of data center equipment through retirement and destruction; Decommissioned Disk multi-step erase policy verified by two independent validators (GDPR resource center; Cloud DPA Appendix 2, 'Decommissioned Disks and Disk Erase Policy')
Dedicated security incident detection and response: Google monitors communication channels for security incidents and security personnel react promptly to known incidents (Cloud DPA Appendix 2)
Customer-controlled key options: Cloud KMS customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK), FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated Cloud HSM, external key manager (Cloud EKM) (Cloud Key Management product page)
Data location controls: services configurable to store data at rest only in a selected region/multi-region; Assured Workloads can restrict data processing and Google personnel access to the selected region, including EU-only processing (Google Cloud Service Terms, 'Data Location' and 'Assured Workloads' sections)
Annual disaster recovery testing (GDPR resource center)' (source: https://cloud.google.com/terms/data-processing-addendum; verdict: disputed). VERIFIER DISPUTED-AND-CORRECTED 2026-07-31: 10 of the researcher's 11 lines verified verbatim against the fetched pages. ONE LINE CORRECTED: the researcher's physical-security line claimed 'access badges, biometric identification, physical locks (Cloud DPA Appendix 2, Section 2(a))' — the CURRENT Cloud DPA text contains none of those three terms (zero grep hits for badge/biometric/lock in the fetched DPA). What Section 2(a) actually states: 24/7 on-site security operation, CCTV inside and outside, electronic card key access with alarms, internal/external patrols, alarmed fire doors, identity verification for all entrants. The line has been rewritten to match the source; likely the researcher quoted an older DPA revision from memory. The media-disposal line was also tightened to the actual mechanisms (asset tracking to destruction on the GDPR page; Decommissioned Disk Erase Policy in the DPA). All other lines confirmed: TLS-by-default (both pages), at-rest-by-default (GDPR page), PFS ECDHE+RSA/ECDSA (DPA verbatim), multi-tenant logical isolation (DPA Section 3(a) verbatim), least-privilege/need-to-know + formal approval (GDPR page verbatim) + hardware tokens (DPA verbatim), incident response (DPA verbatim), CMEK/Cloud HSM FIPS 140-2 L3/Cloud EKM (KMS page verbatim), data location + Assured Workloads EU (Service Terms verbatim), annual DR testing (GDPR page verbatim).
